name: carbon-of-compute
description: Carbon and water footprint estimates for AI language models and AI hardware, from carbonofcompute.com.

interface.longDescription:
Carbon of Compute estimates the greenhouse gas and water footprint of running AI language models, per 1,000 output tokens or per task. Each figure is split into four parts: the electricity the hardware draws, the manufacturing of that hardware spread over its working life, the datacenter facility plant, and optionally a share of model training. Footprint results come with low and high values.

You can ask for one model's footprint, compare several models under the same assumptions, and change the electricity grid region, datacenter efficiency (PUE), hardware lifetime, utilization and cooling regime. The app also returns the manufacturing footprint of AI accelerators (NVIDIA H100, H200, B200, A100, AMD MI300X) split into logic die, HBM memory, package and board; an 8-GPU server line by line; and datacenter facility factors.

Intended for engineers, sustainability analysts, researchers and journalists who need a sourced estimate with its assumptions shown. Footprint and ranking answers link to the same view on carbonofcompute.com and to the method report. Hardware manufacturing figures come from REEL LCI, whose foreground inventory is built from public sources and linked to licensed ecoinvent 3.12 background results.

Limitations: figures are estimates built from public evidence for a reference deployment, not a provider's own measurement of its service. The low-high span is not complete uncertainty. Separately executed routing, safety and tool services are not consistently covered, and the datacenter building shell is excluded. The app only reads published data; it does not take actions or access any account.
defaultPrompt: What is the carbon footprint of Llama 3.3 70B per 1,000 output tokens?
Compare DeepSeek R1 and gpt-oss-120b per coding task on the EU average grid.
How much of an NVIDIA H100's manufacturing carbon comes from its HBM memory?

positive.description: Footprint of one open-weight model at the site defaults
positive.prompt: What is the carbon footprint of Llama 3.3 70B per 1,000 output tokens?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_model_footprint with model llama33_70b and no other inputs. Reports the total gCO2e with its low and high values, the split into operational, hardware manufacturing and facility, states the default scenario (US average grid, PUE 1.15, training excluded) and gives the view_on_site link.

positive.description: Compare three models per coding task on another grid
positive.prompt: Compare DeepSeek R1, Qwen3 235B and gpt-oss-120b for one coding task on the EU average grid.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls rank_models with the three models, grid eu_average and per code_task. Returns them lowest first with totals and ranges, and notes that the figures come from different evidence levels where they do.

positive.prompt: How much of an NVIDIA H100's manufacturing carbon comes from its HBM memory?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_accelerator_manufacturing with accelerator H100. Reports the HBM share (about 52 percent) and the component values in kgCO2e, with the vendor product carbon footprint for comparison.

positive.prompt: Break down the manufacturing carbon of an 8-GPU H100 server line by line.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_server_manufacturing. Lists each host line (CPUs, DRAM, NICs, boards, power supplies, chassis, NVSwitch, network fabric), storage and the eight accelerators, with the server total of about 3,250 kgCO2e.

positive.description: Lowest-carbon open models on a clean grid
positive.prompt: Which open-weight models have the lowest carbon per million output tokens on a clean nuclear grid like France?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls rank_models with weights open, grid france_clean and per 1m_output_tokens. Lists the lowest models first and notes that on a clean grid hardware manufacturing becomes a larger share of the total.

negative.description: Office electricity emissions are outside the app's scope
negative.prompt: Work out my company's Scope 2 emissions from last year's office electricity bill.

negative.description: Travel emissions are outside the app's scope
negative.prompt: What is the carbon footprint of a return flight from Stockholm to New York?

negative.description: The app cannot take actions such as moving or buying compute
negative.prompt: Move my AWS inference workloads to the region with the cleanest grid.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: First release. Read-only tools over the current carbonofcompute.com release: model footprints, model rankings, accelerator, server and facility manufacturing factors, scenario options and a method summary.
